entries.7457983f31793854: The company, together with seven consolidated subsidiaries, is a single-segment company in the medical products business, which holds an exclusive license from MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) for patents related to self-assembling peptide technology and conducts research and development, manufacturing and sales of medical devices and pharmaceuticals based on this technology.
entries.751772594cd74209: A company that develops and manufactures medical devices such as absorbable topical hemostats based on MIT's self-assembling peptide technology, and sells them in Japan, the US and Europe.
entries.78b49437931ad9a5: Business revenue for the fiscal year ended April 2026 was ¥10,886 million (up 57.0% year on year), and by region was ¥6,249 million in the United States, ¥2,595 million in Europe, ¥1,256 million in Japan and ¥783 million in other regions. Sales in the United States, centered on the gastrointestinal endoscopy field, rose sharply, up 98.2% year on year.
entries.8b274b5f788ff919: The Group's only reportable segment, consisting of the Company and 7 consolidated subsidiaries. Having been granted an exclusive license by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in the U.S. for patents related to self-assembling peptide technology, it researches, develops, manufactures and sells medical devices and pharmaceuticals based on this technology. It has a development pipeline in the surgical field (absorbable local hemostat, mucosal elevating agent, post-bleeding prevention agent, adhesion barrier), the tissue regeneration field (wound healing agent, alveolar bone reconstruction material) and the DDS (drug delivery system) field (technology for nucleic acid drugs and others). Depending on the product and region, it either obtains manufacturing and marketing approval itself and sells directly, or commissions manufacturing or sales to overseas partner companies or grants them licenses. Manufacturing of the absorbable local hemostat is commissioned to Fuso Pharmaceutical Industries, Ltd. in Japan and Pharmpure in Germany. Sales are made under an exclusive sales agreement with FUJIFILM Europe B.V. in Europe (gastrointestinal endoscopy field), and through the Company's own direct sales organization in the U.S., Japan and Australia.

entries.e4ca3f2d441e25bd: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended April 2026 was ¥1,335 million, turning from an operating loss of ¥1,156 million in the previous fiscal year, and the company achieved full-year operating profitability from its marketed products for the first time. Ordinary profit of ¥3,971 million and profit attributable to owners of the parent of ¥4,155 million exceed this figure, but the securities report cites the recording of foreign exchange gains of ¥2,661 million on loans to subsidiaries and other items as the main factor.

entries.fddf69d6b16b281c: Based on self-assembling peptide technology licensed on an exclusive basis from MIT, the company develops, manufactures and sells medical devices centered on an absorbable topical hemostat (development code: TDM-621). Manufacturing is outsourced to Fuso Pharmaceutical Industries, Ltd. in Japan and to Pharmpur GMBH in Germany, and sales are made through the company's own direct sales in the United States, Japan and Australia, and in Europe, for hemostats in the field of gastrointestinal endoscopy, through an exclusive distribution agreement with FUJIFILM Europe B.V. Business revenue for the fiscal year ended April 2026 was ¥10,886 million (up 57.0% year on year), and by region was ¥6,249 million in the United States, ¥2,595 million in Europe, ¥1,256 million in Japan and ¥783 million in other regions. As business scale expanded, the company posted an operating profit of ¥1,335 million this fiscal year, turning profitable for the first time with its marketed products. In addition, products other than hemostats, such as mucosal elevation agents and alveolar bone reconstruction materials, are at the development pipeline stage, and in the DDS field the company aims to earn licensing income by providing its technology to pharmaceutical companies rather than commercializing drugs itself.
